messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: realtime-latency-monitor detected p99 latency breach for /v1/generate in hosted-us-west2. p99=2.8s (SLO=1.2s). Several streaming stalls observed. Paging @oncall-sre. Incident ID INC-3167789. https://console.redwood.example/alerts/INC-3167789

oncall-sre: I'm on call and looking. Marking P1. Priya (runtime) and Alex (infra) please join.

Priya K: Seeing the uptick starting ~3167788900. Canary rollout for model v2.3.1 started ~3167788700 — might be related. Checking rollout dashboard now: https://console.redwood.example/rollouts/xxxxx

Alex M: Infra view: GPU pod churn on us-west2-gpu-pool. kube-events show repeated podEvicted/oom_kill and docker restarts. Autoscaler didn't add nodes — hitting soft quota on that region.

Jason L: Customer side: a couple of high-volume customers reported streaming stalls and disconnects. Logs show chunk send timeouts (10s) and retries. No 5xx spikes, mostly timeouts/retries.

Emily R: Quick mitigation options: 1) pause the canary rollout, 2) route traffic for /v1/generate to a lighter model variant (gpt-medium-fp16) while we stabilize, 3) temporarily enable burst capacity on Dedicated pools for us-west2. Which one can we do fastest? :thinking_face:

Priya K: I can flip routing and pause rollout. Doing a quick check on model kernel selector — if the new variant is picking slower kernels under that sequence length distribution, fallback helps. Executing: `/admin rollouts pause v2.3.1 --reason "p99 regression"`

Priya K: Pasting metric query I'm running:
```
# p99 over last 5m for /v1/generate in us-west2
curl -s 'https://metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=p99_latency{api="/v1/generate",region="us-west2"}&range=5m' | jq
```

Alex M: While Priya flips routing, I'm requesting quota burst from cloud team and starting a manual scale of the GPU pool. cmds: `gcloud compute instances add --count=2 --zone=us-west2-a ...` (PMs/infra please ack)

incident-bot: NOTE: automated rollback candidate detected for v2.3.1 (performance regressions). Manual approval required.

Priya K: Routing change applied: /v1/generate -> model=gpt-medium-fp16 for 80% of traffic in us-west2, 20% kept on current for observability. Paused rollout v2.3.1.

Jason L: Seeing immediate improvement in streaming success rate for routed traffic. p99 samples dropping to ~0.95s on fallback. Still monitoring the 20% on canary.

Emily R: Good. I'll notify support to message affected customers: "We're investigating intermittent streaming stalls; traffic routed to a stable model variant while we investigate. No data loss." @support-team

Alex M: New nodes booting, but some existing nodes show GPU driver churn. I've raised a ticket with cloud infra and will cordon the noisy hosts.

Priya K: Next steps for debug: 1) grab traces for stalled requests (trace IDs from logs), 2) compare kernel selection and quantization path used by v2.3.1 vs fallback, 3) check K/V cache hit rates — if cache thrash occurred that can spike tail latency.

Priya K: Querying cache metrics: `curl 'https://metrics.internal/api/query?query=kv_cache_hit_rate{model="v2.3.1"}' | jq` — seeing sudden drop in hit rate aligned with spike.

Jason L: That aligns with streaming stalls — when KV cache misses, first token cost jumps and can trigger timeouts in streaming. Could be a rollout that changed prefix patterns or cache keying.

Emily R: For immediate mitigation we should keep fallback routing until next deploy is validated. Priya, can you schedule a smaller canary with sticky cache warming?

Priya K: Yep. Plan: warm cache with synthetic traffic for v2.3.1 on one canary replica, then ramp. Also we'll force quantization profile to the known-good setting for that model.

oncall-sre: Current status: p99 back to ~0.9s for majority traffic after routing change and scale. Streaming error rate down from 3.2% to 0.4%. Keeping channel open for 30m post-mitigation. Assigning incident to Priya K for follow-up and RCA.

Priya K: I'll own the RCA. Initial hypothesis: rollout changed tokenization/cache key path causing KV cache thrash + kernel selection edge on long sequences -> tail stalls. Will collect traces/logs and sync with infra on driver churn.

Emily R: Thanks team. Support notified customers, cloud quota requested, and infra is cordoning hosts. Leave this thread open and post updates. :white_check_mark:
